title: Tail-Index Inference for Treatment Arms with Covariate-Varying Tail Onset
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 7.0 < field threshold 7.4; salvageable=false. Math review PASS with no findings; sound result achieves subfield.
gap_reasons: The information conclusion is local to a fixed-onset exact-Pareto subexperiment and establishes covariance attainment only in the asymptotic-distribution sense, not global risk efficiency over the full remainder class.
The pointwise extreme-quantile result is solely a lower bound, so it does not deliver an estimator, matched rate, or feasible CEQTE inference result.

The projected paper score is constrained by the restrictive common-index onset model, absence of practical or numerical evidence that covariate-dependent onset adaptation materially changes inference, and the lack of a statement-level priority comparison with Drees–Knežević Lemma C.3 and the cited conditional-tail literature.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a conservative conditional-onset learner, one-sided oracle transfer, and local observed-law information, plus a pointwise extreme-quantile lower bound; the math referee passed with no findings. D0.5 assigned subfield (paper-score ceiling 7.0 below the field threshold 7.4) because the information result is local, the pointwise result has no matching attainable upper bound, and the model and evidence limit the package. The maximal sign-changing threshold-transfer class remains open; a bounded positioning repair cannot reach the field floor.
tldr: Conditional tail entry can vary sharply across mixed covariates even under the maintained scale-only restriction that each treatment arm has a common Pareto index. A stratum-cell empirical quantile, inflated just enough to lie above every conditional onset with high probability, permits cross-fitted pooling of observed armwise log excesses without propensity weighting. The proved package gives a uniform studentized oracle expansion for pilots whose upper log-onset error is nonnegative and uniformly vanishing, certifies the sharp observed-law information \(k\mu_a/\gamma_a^2\), gives a counterexample excluding unrestricted downward or sign-changing extensions when \(\sqrt{k}\epsilon_n\not\to0\), and separates index information from the slower pointwise uncertainty of conditional extreme quantiles. A necessary-and-sufficient transfer class allowing sign-changing threshold errors remains open.
gap: Existing random-threshold theorems are scalar or impose two-sided local tail regularity; conditional tail-index estimators smooth around covariates; published causal Hill and causal Fraga procedures use marginal quantiles with inverse-propensity weighting. None of the verified comparators gives a feasible uniformly conservative covariate-dependent onset learner together with no-prescribed-rate oracle transfer, studentization, and an observed-law causal information bound when the lower body is unrestricted.
fill: The project supplies the conditional empirical-quantile pilot, the survival-integral transfer argument, joint feasible inference, and the fixed-onset local likelihood experiment. The downward-error construction is an internal necessity boundary for the one-sided theorem, and the pointwise extreme-quantile lower floor prevents an overbroad downstream variance claim.
